voyage.name: MADD-Musée des Arts décoratifs et du Design de Bordeaux
Cathédrale St-André
voyage.content: Grand church built from 1170 in Gothic style. It was trashed during the Revolution but restored from 1803. You can climb the detached bell-tower "Pey-Berland".

voyage.name: Musée des Beaux-Arts
voyage.content: An enlightening walk through the history of western art. Start in the south wing which runs from the Renaissance via the Flemish masters to end of 18th century. The north wing continues through the major 19th and early 20th-century art movements. Exhibitions are in the annexe, Galerie des Beaux-Arts, on Place du Colonel Raynal 200 m north.

voyage.name: Musée National des Douanes
voyage.content: Surprisingly informative museum of border control and customs, and their smuggler opponents, down the centuries. Signage only in French, non-francophones should get the audioguide.

voyage.name: Basilique Saint-Michel
voyage.content: Flamboyant Gothic church built from the 14th to 16th century, with detached bell-tower.

voyage.name: Église Sainte-Croix
voyage.content: This was built in the 11th / 12th century as a Benedictine abbey church, and was renovated in the 19th.

voyage.name: Musée D'Aquitaine
voyage.content: Brilliant museum with exhibits from the Old Stone Age through Roman times to the early modern period.

voyage.name: Musée d'Art Contemporain
voyage.content: Remarkable building, the Entrepôt Lainé is a huge 19th warehouse for food imports. Most of the space is given over to changing exhibitions and installations (and prices are reduced whenever there isn't one). Display of the permanent collection also rotates.

voyage.name: Musée du Vin et du Négoce
voyage.content: History, old equipment and new technology from 2000 years of wine production in the region. The entry fee includes a taste of two wines. (grape juice for children)

voyage.name: Musée Mer Marine
voyage.hours: Tue-Sun 13:00-19:00 (opens at 10:30 during French school holidays)
voyage.content: Extensive museum of shipping and the sea.

voyage.name: Base sous-marine
voyage.content: Wartime submarine pens, now used for art installations.

voyage.name: Jardin Botanique du Jardin Publique
voyage.content: Started as a garden of medicinal herbs in 1629, the present garden dates from 1858 and covers 0.5 ha. This is the original now specified as "du Jardin Publique". In 2003 an offshoot garden de la Bastide was opened across the river.

voyage.name: Muséum de Bordeaux - sciences et nature
voyage.content: Extensive natural history museum on three floors.

voyage.name: Jeux Barjo
voyage.content: Bar specialising in board games ancient and modern: you pay for either one long or three short games. Staff assist if you want to try a game you're not familiar with. They also stage tournaments.

voyage.name: Chat Noir Cha Vert
voyage.content: Pleasant place for light bites and views of the basilica.

voyage.name: Beirut Kitchen
voyage.content: Good mezze and other Levantine fare.

voyage.name: Chez Ta Mère
voyage.content: As the name suggests, they serve rustic home-style cuisine.

voyage.name: Remparts Café
voyage.content: Charming bistro a few steps from the cathedral.

voyage.name: L'Autre Petit Bois
voyage.content: Quirky sandwich cafe, generous portions, gets crowded.

voyage.name: Café Populaire
voyage.content: Relaxed restaurant, then it morphs into a dad-dancing arena.

voyage.name: Le Café du Port
voyage.content: Great views of Pont de Pierre and the left riverbank. Good dining to match, they often host events.

voyage.name: L'entrecôte
voyage.content: A city institution, no reservations and you'll probably have a long wait in line. What you get is a walnut salad, two pieces of entrecôte steak and unlimited fries, plus dessert and wine. Most customers reckon it's worth the wait.

voyage.name: Couleur Cafe
voyage.address: 28 Rue du Pere Louis de Jabrun
voyage.content: Mostly positive reviews for this bistro by the cathedral.

voyage.name: Chez Faty
voyage.content: Delicious lunchtime couscous and tajine.

voyage.name: MAMACAM
voyage.content: Food made with local products. Always vegetarian options.

voyage.name: Restaurant Soléna
voyage.content: Outstanding French / Oriental cuisine. The chef is Victor Ostronzec.

voyage.name: La Tupina
voyage.content: Great regional cuisine and friendly service in a bistro ambiance, try the corn-fed Landes fowl.

voyage.name: L'Estacade
voyage.content: Great food and views in a building jutting over the water on stilts, reservations recommended.

voyage.name: Dick Turpin's
voyage.content: English style pub with good drink and music, relaxed friendly vibe.

voyage.name: El Chuchumbe
voyage.content: Latin bar serving inexpensive mojitos, and towards midnight it becomes a salsa dance floor.

voyage.name: The Frog and Rosbif
voyage.content: English pub with micro-brewery in a 16th century women's prison, a popular gathering spot for live TV sports.

voyage.name: Le Café Brun
voyage.content: Atmospheric old bar with a huge selection of whiskies and Belgian beers.

voyage.name: Brique House Bordeaux
voyage.content: Originally from Lille this popular Taproom-restaurant is now in Bordeaux.

voyage.name: Space Factory
voyage.content: Craft beer bar

voyage.name: L'Auberge Barbey
voyage.content: Bordeaux's only hostel was refurbished in 2024. They have ten rooms with two beds, 17 with four and three with six. No access to rooms 11:00-16:00.

voyage.name: Ibis Budget Bordeaux Centre Gare St Jean
voyage.content: Basic chain offering, rooms are small but clean and comfy.

voyage.name: Ibis Bordeaux Centre Gare St Jean Euratlantique
voyage.content: Great location within the station building.

voyage.name: Ibis Styles Bordeaux Centre Gare St Jean
voyage.content: The most disappointing of the set, rooms were too often grubby.

voyage.name: Ibis Bordeaux Centre Gare St Jean
voyage.content: Quiet convenient chain offering.

voyage.name: Best Western Plus Hôtel Gare Saint-Jean
voyage.content: Comfy but some street noise.

voyage.name: Best Western Premier Hotel
voyage.content: Charming 18th-century hotel, with fine furnishings throughout the hotel, with mahogany furnishings and beech furniture. Close to the Grand Theatre and the Triangle d'Or.

voyage.name: Hotel de Normandie
voyage.content: Great comfort and service, and views of the Place des Quinconces.

voyage.name: Hilton Garden Inn
voyage.content: Smart new hotel near the river, a 30-minute walk to the historic city center. There's also a food court nearby.

voyage.name: A Blue Lodge in Bordeaux
voyage.content: Lovely friendly 19th century guesthouse with garden, near universities and Victoire.

voyage.name: InterContinental
voyage.content: Five-star hotel by the opera house, run by IHG group. They're going for the old look, which in places feels a bit worn.

voyage.name: Novotel Bordeaux Lac
voyage.content: Comfy place with pool besides Bordeaux lake, near the Convention centre.

voyage.name: Hotel Indigo Bordeaux Centre Chartrons
voyage.content: Smart business hotel on Quais near the congress centre.
